paragraphs.title: Warning About Entering the Holy Place

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
Aaron
Aaron’s two sons
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “The Lord spoke unto Moses.”

easy.question: Who died before this warning was given to Aaron?
answers: Moses and Aaron
Aaron’s two sons
All the priests
easy.explanation: The passage mentions the death of Aaron’s two sons.

easy.question: To whom was Moses told to speak in verse 2?
answers: The Israelites
Aaron’s two sons
Aaron his brother
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses, “Speak unto Aaron thy brother.”

medium.question: What happened before the Lord gave Moses instructions for Aaron?
answers: Aaron’s two sons died when they approached the Lord
Aaron entered the holy place safely
Moses built the ark
medium.explanation: The passage first recalls the death of Aaron’s two sons.

medium.question: Why was Aaron told not to enter the holy place at all times?
answers: The holy place was always closed
So that he would not die, because the Lord appeared there in a cloud
Only Moses was allowed to speak with the Lord
medium.explanation: Aaron’s entry was restricted so that he would not die, since the Lord appeared in the cloud over the mercy seat.

medium.question: In the phrase “within the veil,” what does “veil” refer to?
answers: A vessel for sacrifices
A cloud covering the mercy seat
A curtain separating the inner holy area
medium.explanation: The verse describes the place beyond the curtain separating the holy areas.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “that he come not at all times into the holy place”?
answers: Entry was restricted and not permitted at every time
Aaron was never allowed to enter
Anyone could enter whenever he wished
challenge.explanation: “At all times” prohibits unrestricted entry, not every possible entry.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that the mercy seat was above the ark?
answers: “Before the mercy seat”
“Upon the ark”
“After the death of Aaron’s two sons”
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the mercy seat was “upon the ark.”

challenge.question: What connection between the death of Aaron’s sons and the warning to Aaron is suggested?
answers: Their death made the holy place more accessible
Their death showed that all priests had to stop serving
Their death shows that entering the holy place improperly could be dangerous
challenge.explanation: Their death is mentioned immediately before Aaron is warned about entering improperly.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “that he come not at all times into the holy place”?
answers: Entry was restricted and not permitted at every time
Aaron was never allowed to enter
Anyone could enter whenever he wished
questions.explanation: “At all times” prohibits unrestricted entry, not every possible entry.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that the mercy seat was above the ark?
answers: “Before the mercy seat”
“Upon the ark”
“After the death of Aaron’s two sons”
questions.explanation: The verse says that the mercy seat was “upon the ark.”

questions.question: What connection between the death of Aaron’s sons and the warning to Aaron is suggested?
answers: Their death made the holy place more accessible
Their death showed that all priests had to stop serving
Their death shows that entering the holy place improperly could be dangerous
questions.explanation: Their death is mentioned immediately before Aaron is warned about entering improperly.

paragraphs.title: Preparing the Priest and the Offerings

easy.question: With which animals was Aaron to enter the holy place?
answers: A young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering
Two goats
Two rams
easy.explanation: Aaron was to bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

easy.question: What material were Aaron’s holy garments made of?
answers: Wool
Linen
Leather
easy.explanation: The garments are repeatedly described as linen.

easy.question: Who provided the two goats?
answers: Aaron
The priests
The congregation of Israel
easy.explanation: The goats were taken from the congregation of Israel.

medium.question: What did Aaron do before putting on the holy garments?
answers: He brought two rams
He washed his flesh with water
He took the goats
medium.explanation: Aaron washed his flesh with water and then put on the garments.

medium.question: What does “mitre” mean in “the linen mitre”?
answers: A belt
Trousers
A head covering
medium.explanation: The verse lists the mitre among the garments worn on the head.

medium.question: Which offering came from the congregation of Israel rather than from Aaron?
answers: The two goats for a sin offering
Aaron’s young bull for a sin offering
Aaron’s ram for a burnt offering
medium.explanation: The congregation provided the two goats, while Aaron brought his own bull and ram.

challenge.question: What do the words “holy garments,” together with Aaron’s washing, suggest?
answers: The garments were for all the people
Entering the holy place required special preparation
The garments were made of expensive material
challenge.explanation: The holy garments and washing emphasize preparation for sacred service.

challenge.question: How many rams are mentioned in verses 3–5 altogether?
answers: One
Two
Three
challenge.explanation: Aaron brought one ram, and the congregation brought another.

challenge.question: What does “of the congregation of the children of Israel” emphasize about the offerings?
answers: They came from another country
Only Aaron could choose them
The congregation supplied them
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the congregation as the source of the offerings.

questions.question: What do the words “holy garments,” together with Aaron’s washing, suggest?
answers: The garments were for all the people
Entering the holy place required special preparation
The garments were made of expensive material
questions.explanation: The holy garments and washing emphasize preparation for sacred service.

questions.question: How many rams are mentioned in verses 3–5 altogether?
answers: One
Two
Three
questions.explanation: Aaron brought one ram, and the congregation brought another.

questions.question: What does “of the congregation of the children of Israel” emphasize about the offerings?
answers: They came from another country
Only Aaron could choose them
The congregation supplied them
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies the congregation as the source of the offerings.

paragraphs.title: The Two Goats and the Lots

easy.question: What did Aaron offer at the beginning of the process?
answers: His bull for a sin offering
The scapegoat
A ram for a burnt offering
easy.explanation: Aaron offered his bull as a sin offering.

easy.question: How many goats did Aaron take?
answers: One
Two
Three
easy.explanation: The passage says that he took two goats.

easy.question: Where did Aaron place the two goats?
answers: Outside the camp
In the wilderness
Before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The goats were presented before the Lord at the tabernacle entrance.

medium.question: What did Aaron do before casting lots for the goats?
answers: He presented them before the Lord
He sent them into the wilderness
He offered both of them
medium.explanation: Aaron first presented the goats before the Lord.

medium.question: For whom did Aaron make atonement with his bull?
answers: Only the wilderness people
For himself and his household
For the scapegoat
medium.explanation: The bull made atonement for Aaron and his household.

medium.question: What were the lots used to determine?
answers: Special clothing
The goats’ horns
The role assigned to each goat
medium.explanation: The lots determined which goat was for the Lord and which was the scapegoat.

challenge.question: What different results did the two lots produce?
answers: One goat was offered as a sin offering, and the other remained alive and was sent away
Both goats were offered as sin offerings
Both goats were sent into the wilderness
challenge.explanation: One lot designated a goat for the Lord; the other designated the live scapegoat.

challenge.question: What was distinctive about the goat chosen as the scapegoat?
answers: It was offered immediately before the Lord
It remained alive before the Lord and was then sent into the wilderness
It was returned to Aaron’s household
challenge.explanation: The scapegoat was presented alive and later sent into the wilderness.

challenge.question: What does “the goat upon which the lot fell” mean?
answers: The goat climbed to a high place
The goat was above the lot
The lot assigned that goat a particular role
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the result of the casting of lots.

questions.question: What different results did the two lots produce?
answers: One goat was offered as a sin offering, and the other remained alive and was sent away
Both goats were offered as sin offerings
Both goats were sent into the wilderness
questions.explanation: One lot designated a goat for the Lord; the other designated the live scapegoat.

questions.question: What was distinctive about the goat chosen as the scapegoat?
answers: It was offered immediately before the Lord
It remained alive before the Lord and was then sent into the wilderness
It was returned to Aaron’s household
questions.explanation: The scapegoat was presented alive and later sent into the wilderness.

questions.question: What does “the goat upon which the lot fell” mean?
answers: The goat climbed to a high place
The goat was above the lot
The lot assigned that goat a particular role
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the result of the casting of lots.

paragraphs.title: The Incense and the Bull’s Blood

easy.question: What did Aaron do with his bull for a sin offering?
answers: He offered it and made atonement for himself and his household
He gave it to the people
He hid it behind the veil
easy.explanation: Aaron offered the bull to make atonement for himself and his household.

easy.question: What did Aaron take from the altar?
answers: Blood and wine
Burning coals and incense
Water and oil
easy.explanation: He took burning coals and incense.

easy.question: How many times did Aaron sprinkle blood before the mercy seat?
answers: Once
Three times
Seven times
easy.explanation: The blood was sprinkled seven times before the mercy seat.

medium.question: What did Aaron do after slaughtering the bull?
answers: He took coals and incense and brought them within the veil
He immediately left the tabernacle
He sprinkled the blood on the people
medium.explanation: After slaughtering the bull, he brought coals and incense within the veil.

medium.question: What is a censer in “a censer full of burning coals”?
answers: A bowl for eating
A container for carrying coals
A special garment
medium.explanation: A censer is a vessel used to hold burning coals.

medium.question: Why did Aaron put the incense on the fire?
answers: So its cloud would cover the mercy seat
To put out the altar fire
To prepare the bull for eating
medium.explanation: The incense created a cloud covering the mercy seat so Aaron would not die.

challenge.question: For whom did Aaron make atonement with his bull?
answers: For himself and his household
For all nations
For the priests only
challenge.explanation: The bull made atonement for Aaron and his household.

challenge.question: How many sprinklings of blood are described in verse 14 altogether?
answers: Seven
Eight
Fourteen
challenge.explanation: There was one sprinkling on the mercy seat and seven before it.

challenge.question: What detail is shared by both sprinklings in verse 14?
answers: Both were done with a vessel
Both were done outside the tabernacle
Both were done with Aaron’s finger
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Aaron sprinkled the blood with his finger in both actions.

questions.question: For whom did Aaron make atonement with his bull?
answers: For himself and his household
For all nations
For the priests only
questions.explanation: The bull made atonement for Aaron and his household.

questions.question: How many sprinklings of blood are described in verse 14 altogether?
answers: Seven
Eight
Fourteen
questions.explanation: There was one sprinkling on the mercy seat and seven before it.

questions.question: What detail is shared by both sprinklings in verse 14?
answers: Both were done with a vessel
Both were done outside the tabernacle
Both were done with Aaron’s finger
questions.explanation: The verse says that Aaron sprinkled the blood with his finger in both actions.

paragraphs.title: Atonement and Cleansing of the Sanctuary

easy.question: Which animal was killed as the sin offering in verse 15?
answers: The goat for the people
A ram
A lamb
easy.explanation: The verse says that Aaron killed the goat of the sin offering for the people.

easy.question: How many times was blood sprinkled on the altar?
answers: Twice
Seven times
Ten times
easy.explanation: The blood was sprinkled seven times.

easy.question: Who was not to be in the tabernacle during the atonement?
answers: The high priest
The whole congregation
Anyone
easy.explanation: The passage says that no person was to be in the tabernacle until Aaron came out.

medium.question: What is the correct order in verses 15–16?
answers: Go to the altar, kill the goat, then bring in the blood
Kill the goat, bring its blood inside, and sprinkle it
Sprinkle the altar, cleanse the people, then kill the goat
medium.explanation: The goat was killed, its blood was brought within the veil, and the blood was sprinkled.

medium.question: What does “make an atonement for the holy place” mean here?
answers: Build it
Hide it
Cleanse it from the people’s uncleanness and sins
medium.explanation: The ritual cleansed the holy place from the uncleanness and sins of Israel.

medium.question: Why was atonement made for both the holy place and the tabernacle?
answers: The Israelites lived among them even while unclean and sinful
They were outside the camp
They were used only for thank offerings
medium.explanation: The Lord’s dwelling was among Israel, including while they were in their uncleanness.

challenge.question: What blood was placed on the horns of the altar?
answers: The blood of the bull and the goat
Only the bull’s blood
Water and oil
challenge.explanation: The verse says that blood from both the bull and the goat was placed on the altar’s horns.

challenge.question: For whom did the priest make atonement according to verse 17?
answers: Only himself
Himself, his household, and the whole congregation of Israel
The priests only
challenge.explanation: The verse names Aaron, his household, and all Israel.

challenge.question: What does the movement from the holy place to the altar suggest?
answers: The altar was unrelated to atonement
The work ended after the goat was killed
Atonement involved cleansing several sacred places
challenge.explanation: Atonement was made for the holy place, the tabernacle, and then the altar.

questions.question: What blood was placed on the horns of the altar?
answers: The blood of the bull and the goat
Only the bull’s blood
Water and oil
questions.explanation: The verse says that blood from both the bull and the goat was placed on the altar’s horns.

questions.question: For whom did the priest make atonement according to verse 17?
answers: Only himself
Himself, his household, and the whole congregation of Israel
The priests only
questions.explanation: The verse names Aaron, his household, and all Israel.

questions.question: What does the movement from the holy place to the altar suggest?
answers: The altar was unrelated to atonement
The work ended after the goat was killed
Atonement involved cleansing several sacred places
questions.explanation: Atonement was made for the holy place, the tabernacle, and then the altar.

paragraphs.title: Confession and Sending Away the Goat

easy.question: Who laid both hands on the head of the live goat?
answers: Aaron
The fit man
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says that Aaron laid both hands on the goat.

easy.question: Where was the live goat sent?
answers: To the tabernacle
Into the wilderness
To the altar
easy.explanation: The goat was sent into the wilderness.

easy.question: What did the goat carry?
answers: The holy vessels
The priests’ offerings
The iniquities of the Israelites
easy.explanation: The goat carried all their iniquities into an uninhabited land.

medium.question: What happened after atonement was made for the holy place, tabernacle, and altar?
answers: The goat was immediately sent away
The live goat was brought forward
Aaron left the camp
medium.explanation: After the atonement, Aaron brought the live goat.

medium.question: What does “a fit man” mean in this passage?
answers: A young man
A stranger
A man prepared or appointed for the task
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the person chosen and prepared to lead the goat away.

medium.question: What resulted from confessing the sins over the goat?
answers: The goat carried them away into the wilderness
The goat remained in the tabernacle
The sins were written on the altar
medium.explanation: The goat bore the people’s iniquities and was sent into the wilderness.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Aaron laying both hands on the goat?
answers: The action was secret
The action was deliberate and complete
The goat had two heads
challenge.explanation: The detail emphasizes a deliberate act connected with confession and transfer.

challenge.question: What does “putting them upon the head of the goat” refer to?
answers: All the iniquities and sins previously confessed
Aaron’s two hands
The holy vessels
challenge.explanation: “Them” refers to the iniquities, transgressions, and sins of Israel.

challenge.question: What distinguishes this goat from the goat offered in the holy place?
answers: This live goat was taken to the altar
This live goat was sent into the wilderness carrying the sins
This live goat remained in the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The goat remained alive, carried the people’s sins, and was sent away.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Aaron laying both hands on the goat?
answers: The action was secret
The action was deliberate and complete
The goat had two heads
questions.explanation: The detail emphasizes a deliberate act connected with confession and transfer.

questions.question: What does “putting them upon the head of the goat” refer to?
answers: All the iniquities and sins previously confessed
Aaron’s two hands
The holy vessels
questions.explanation: “Them” refers to the iniquities, transgressions, and sins of Israel.

questions.question: What distinguishes this goat from the goat offered in the holy place?
answers: This live goat was taken to the altar
This live goat was sent into the wilderness carrying the sins
This live goat remained in the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The goat remained alive, carried the people’s sins, and was sent away.

easy.question: What did Aaron do with the linen garments after leaving the holy place?
answers: He left them in the tabernacle
He burned them outside the camp
He gave them to the man who sent away the goat
easy.explanation: Aaron removed the linen garments and left them in the tabernacle.

easy.question: What did Aaron do after putting on his regular garments?
answers: He went outside the camp
He offered his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering
He sent away the scapegoat
easy.explanation: Aaron put on his garments and offered the burnt offerings.

easy.question: What was required of the person who burned the sin offerings?
answers: He had to remain outside the camp
He had to wear linen garments
He had to wash his clothes and bathe
easy.explanation: He had to wash his clothes and bathe his flesh in water.

medium.question: Why did Aaron wash and put on his garments before offering the burnt offerings?
answers: To prepare for the rest of his service
To prepare the scapegoat
To burn the linen garments
medium.explanation: After his work in the holy place, Aaron washed, dressed, and continued the service.

medium.question: What does “he that let go the goat” mean?
answers: The person who sacrificed the goat
The person who sent the goat away
The person who burned the goat
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the person who released and sent away the goat.

medium.question: What was the correct order for the person who sent away the goat?
answers: Wash, send the goat, then wash clothes
Send the goat, wash clothes and bathe, then return to the camp
Return to camp, send the goat, then wash
medium.explanation: He sent away the goat, washed and bathed, and then returned to the camp.

challenge.question: What distinguishes Aaron from the person who sent away the goat?
answers: Aaron changed garments before the burnt offerings, while the other man washed afterward
Aaron burned the sin offerings, while the other burned the fat
Aaron stayed outside the camp, while the other entered the holy place
challenge.explanation: Aaron changed garments before the offerings; the other man washed after sending away the goat.

challenge.question: Why were the bull and goat taken outside the camp?
answers: They were intended for the priests to eat
Their blood had been brought into the holy place, so their bodies were burned outside the camp
They could not be brought into the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: Because their blood was used in the holy place, their bodies were taken outside and burned.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the washing required of both men?
answers: Their special duties required cleansing before they returned to the camp
They were the only priests serving that day
They had to wear Aaron’s linen garments
challenge.explanation: Both performed special duties connected with the Day of Atonement and had to cleanse themselves.

questions.question: What distinguishes Aaron from the person who sent away the goat?
answers: Aaron changed garments before the burnt offerings, while the other man washed afterward
Aaron burned the sin offerings, while the other burned the fat
Aaron stayed outside the camp, while the other entered the holy place
questions.explanation: Aaron changed garments before the offerings; the other man washed after sending away the goat.

questions.question: Why were the bull and goat taken outside the camp?
answers: They were intended for the priests to eat
Their blood had been brought into the holy place, so their bodies were burned outside the camp
They could not be brought into the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Because their blood was used in the holy place, their bodies were taken outside and burned.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the washing required of both men?
answers: Their special duties required cleansing before they returned to the camp
They were the only priests serving that day
They had to wear Aaron’s linen garments
questions.explanation: Both performed special duties connected with the Day of Atonement and had to cleanse themselves.

paragraphs.title: The Day of Atonement and the People’s Cleansing

easy.question: When was this command to be observed?
answers: On the tenth day of the seventh month
On the first day of the first month
On the fifteenth day of the third month
easy.explanation: The command was for the tenth day of the seventh month.

easy.question: What were the people forbidden to do?
answers: Eat bread
Do any work
Speak to one another
easy.explanation: The verse says, “do no work at all.”

easy.question: Who was included in this command?
answers: The priests only
Israelites in the land only
The native-born and the stranger living among them
easy.explanation: The verse includes both the native-born and the stranger living among them.

medium.question: Why were the people to afflict themselves and do no work?
answers: Because the priest would make atonement and cleanse them
Because it was New Year’s Day
Because it was harvest time
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the priest would make atonement and cleanse the people.

medium.question: What does “afflict your souls” mean here?
answers: Rejoice greatly
Humble or discipline yourselves, such as by fasting
Answer someone who asks a question
medium.explanation: The context indicates self-denial and fasting, not answering a question.

medium.question: What is the main sequence of ideas in these verses?
answers: Work, celebration, and then atonement
Cleansing, work, and then self-denial
Self-denial and no work, followed by atonement and cleansing
medium.explanation: The command comes first, followed by the explanation that the day brings cleansing from sin.

challenge.question: What does “a statute for ever” emphasize?
answers: The command was established for all generations
The command was observed only once
The command applied only to the high priest
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a permanent, ongoing statute.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from mentioning both the native-born and the stranger?
answers: Only the stranger was obligated
The command applied to Israelites and resident foreigners alike
The stranger could work that day
challenge.explanation: Both groups are included in the same command.

challenge.question: What does “all your sins” emphasize?
answers: Atonement was for only one sin
Cleansing depended on doing work
The cleansing covered every sin
challenge.explanation: The wording indicates comprehensive cleansing from sin.

questions.question: What does “a statute for ever” emphasize?
answers: The command was established for all generations
The command was observed only once
The command applied only to the high priest
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a permanent, ongoing statute.

questions.question: What can be inferred from mentioning both the native-born and the stranger?
answers: Only the stranger was obligated
The command applied to Israelites and resident foreigners alike
The stranger could work that day
questions.explanation: Both groups are included in the same command.

questions.question: What does “all your sins” emphasize?
answers: Atonement was for only one sin
Cleansing depended on doing work
The cleansing covered every sin
questions.explanation: The wording indicates comprehensive cleansing from sin.

paragraphs.title: A Sabbath of Rest and Self-Denial

easy.question: What does the verse command the people to do?
answers: Rest and afflict themselves
Build an altar
Go to war
easy.explanation: The day was to be a Sabbath of rest, and the people were to afflict themselves.

easy.question: To whom is the command addressed?
answers: The priests only
You
The king only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you.”

easy.question: How is the day described?
answers: As a day of war
As a day of celebration
As a Sabbath of rest
easy.explanation: The verse calls it “a sabbath of rest.”

medium.question: What is the relationship between “a Sabbath of rest” and “afflict your souls”?
answers: It is a day of rest together with self-denial
It is a day of hard work
It is a day when everything is permitted
medium.explanation: The verse combines special rest with self-denial.

medium.question: What does “afflict your souls” mean in this verse?
answers: Sing aloud
Deny yourselves and limit bodily pleasures
Go on a journey
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to self-denial and restraint.

medium.question: What follows from calling it “a statute for ever”?
answers: The command applied for only one day
The command depended on each person’s choice
The command was established permanently
medium.explanation: “A statute for ever” indicates a lasting command.

challenge.question: Which phrase most strongly emphasizes the extent of the rest?
answers: “A Sabbath of rest”
“Unto you”
“Your souls”
challenge.explanation: The repeated idea of Sabbath rest emphasizes special and complete rest.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from commanding both rest and self-denial?
answers: The day was only for physical activity
The day required stopping work and practicing restraint
The rest canceled all other commands
challenge.explanation: The two commands require both cessation from work and personal discipline.

challenge.question: What detail might be missed when reading quickly?
answers: The command is addressed to many people
The verse discusses building the tabernacle
The statute is limited to the high priest
challenge.explanation: The verse addresses the people generally and calls the command a permanent statute.

questions.question: Which phrase most strongly emphasizes the extent of the rest?
answers: “A Sabbath of rest”
“Unto you”
“Your souls”
questions.explanation: The repeated idea of Sabbath rest emphasizes special and complete rest.

questions.question: What can be inferred from commanding both rest and self-denial?
answers: The day was only for physical activity
The day required stopping work and practicing restraint
The rest canceled all other commands
questions.explanation: The two commands require both cessation from work and personal discipline.

questions.question: What detail might be missed when reading quickly?
answers: The command is addressed to many people
The verse discusses building the tabernacle
The statute is limited to the high priest
questions.explanation: The verse addresses the people generally and calls the command a permanent statute.

paragraphs.title: The High Priest in the Holy Garments

easy.question: Who makes atonement according to the verse?
answers: The priest
The king
The Levites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the priest ... shall make the atonement.”

easy.question: What does the priest wear?
answers: Wool garments
Linen garments, the holy garments
Royal garments
easy.explanation: The priest wears linen clothes, identified as holy garments.

easy.question: Whose place does the priest serve in?
answers: The king’s
His brother’s
His father’s
easy.explanation: The priest ministers in his father’s stead.

medium.question: Which description matches the priest in this verse?
answers: He is anointed, consecrated, and serves in his father’s place
He is chosen by the people and wears royal garments
He is a Levite forbidden to enter the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The verse describes an anointed and consecrated priest serving in his father’s stead.

medium.question: What does “consecrate him to minister in the priest’s office” mean?
answers: Give his hand to another person
Prepare and appoint him for priestly service
Wash his hands before serving
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to being prepared and appointed for priestly service.

medium.question: What does “in his father’s stead” mean?
answers: He serves in his father’s place or continues his role
He must stand beneath his father
He works only in his father’s house
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates succession to his father’s priestly role.

challenge.question: What does the combination of being anointed and consecrated emphasize?
answers: The priest received both anointing and training for the office
The priest was chosen only because of his age
The priest wore only two kinds of clothing
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions both anointing and consecration as aspects of entering the office.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from calling the linen clothes “holy garments”?
answers: They were made of gold
They were special garments for sacred service
They were ordinary clothing
challenge.explanation: The wording identifies the linen garments as dedicated to holy service.

challenge.question: Which statement best matches the verse?
answers: Anyone could become a priest by wearing linen
The office depended only on clothing
A priest succeeding his father had to be consecrated and wear holy garments
challenge.explanation: The verse connects priestly appointment, succession, and holy garments.

questions.question: What does the combination of being anointed and consecrated emphasize?
answers: The priest received both anointing and training for the office
The priest was chosen only because of his age
The priest wore only two kinds of clothing
questions.explanation: The verse mentions both anointing and consecration as aspects of entering the office.

questions.question: What can be inferred from calling the linen clothes “holy garments”?
answers: They were made of gold
They were special garments for sacred service
They were ordinary clothing
questions.explanation: The wording identifies the linen garments as dedicated to holy service.

questions.question: Which statement best matches the verse?
answers: Anyone could become a priest by wearing linen
The office depended only on clothing
A priest succeeding his father had to be consecrated and wear holy garments
questions.explanation: The verse connects priestly appointment, succession, and holy garments.

paragraphs.title: Atonement for the Sanctuary and the People

easy.question: For whom was atonement to be made?
answers: The priests and all the people
The kings only
Foreigners only
easy.explanation: The verse mentions the priests and all the congregation.

easy.question: What main verb is repeated in the verse?
answers: Build
Make atonement
Guard
easy.explanation: The verb “make atonement” is repeated several times.

easy.question: Which place is mentioned?
answers: The king’s house
The city gate
The tabernacle of the congregation
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the tabernacle.

medium.question: What is the order of the places and groups mentioned?
answers: The people, priests, altar, tabernacle, and sanctuary
The holy sanctuary, tabernacle, altar, priests, and all the people
The altar, people, tabernacle, priests, and sanctuary
medium.explanation: This is the order in which the verse lists the places and people receiving atonement.

medium.question: What does “the congregation” mean in this verse?
answers: Only a group of priests
A holy place
The assembled community
medium.explanation: Here it refers to the gathered community of Israel.

medium.question: What does mentioning both holy places and people suggest?
answers: Atonement covered both the sacred sphere and the community
Only the places received atonement
Only the priests received atonement
medium.explanation: The verse includes the sanctuary, tabernacle, altar, priests, and people.

challenge.question: Which list contains all the places named in the verse?
answers: The sanctuary, city, and gate
The tabernacle, palace, and courtyard
The holy sanctuary, tabernacle, and altar
challenge.explanation: These are the three places explicitly named.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “make atonement” emphasize?
answers: Atonement applied to several places and groups
Atonement happened only once
The verse concerns only the altar
challenge.explanation: The repetition highlights the broad scope of the atonement.

challenge.question: What detail might be missed when reading quickly?
answers: The priests are not mentioned
The altar is included among the things receiving atonement
The tabernacle is not mentioned
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly includes the altar along with the sanctuary and tabernacle.

questions.question: Which list contains all the places named in the verse?
answers: The sanctuary, city, and gate
The tabernacle, palace, and courtyard
The holy sanctuary, tabernacle, and altar
questions.explanation: These are the three places explicitly named.

easy.question: How is the command described?
answers: As an everlasting statute
As a one-time command
As a recommendation
easy.explanation: The verse calls it an everlasting statute.

easy.question: How often was the atonement to be made?
answers: Every month
Once a year
Only once
easy.explanation: The verse says it was to be done once a year.

easy.question: Who commanded Moses?
answers: The Israelites
The priests
The Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says, “as the Lord commanded Moses.”

medium.question: What was the purpose of the action described in the verse?
answers: To celebrate the beginning of the year
To make atonement for the sins of the Israelites
To count the Israelites
medium.explanation: The verse says it was to make atonement for all their sins.

medium.question: What does “statute” mean in “an everlasting statute”?
answers: A story from the past
A question to investigate
A fixed command or law
medium.explanation: In this context, “statute” means a permanent command.

medium.question: What is the relationship between “once a year” and “everlasting statute”?
answers: The command was permanent and carried out annually
It was done only once
It changed every year
medium.explanation: The statute continued permanently, while its observance took place once each year.

challenge.question: What does “this shall be” refer to in the verse?
answers: One particular year
The atonement procedure described in the chapter
Moses alone
challenge.explanation: “This” refers to the atonement procedure described in the preceding verses.

challenge.question: What does “everlasting statute” together with “once a year” mean?
answers: The law applied for only one generation
The action happened every day
The obligation continued through the generations and was performed annually
challenge.explanation: “Everlasting” indicates duration, while “once a year” indicates frequency.

challenge.question: What does the ending “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The action was carried out according to divine command
The action was Moses’ personal idea
The action was performed without instructions
challenge.explanation: The ending stresses obedience to the Lord’s command.
